Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.

1. Heard Shri Omvir Singh Rajpoot, learned counsel for the petitioners, Shri Pawan Kumar Shukla,
learned counsel for the informant and Shri Ratan Singh, learned AGA for the State-respondents.

2. This writ petition has been filed for quashing the impugned First Information Report No. 0589 of 2023, u/s 420, 406 and 506 IPC, registered at Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad dated 05.08.2023.

sentences.text: The prosecution case is that there is a civil dispute pending between the parties regarding a piece of land situated in District Sambhal, a civil case is also pending disposal in the District Court.
Apprehending defeat in the civil cases, the petitioners hatched a conspiracy to cause unlawful loss to the complainant in the guise of settling the matter finally.
The petitioner offered registration of the sale deed of the half portion of the disputed land in the name of the complainant, subject to payment of Rs. Ninty lakhs.
As per the settlement, the complainant paid Rs. Eighty-Seven Lakhs to petitioners, namely Anand Pal Singh, Harsh Kumar and Hukum Singh, in their respective accounts on various dates through RTGS.
After receipt of the aforesaid amount, the petitioners turned dishonest and refused to register the sale deed, as agreed.
Therefore, the complainant registered the aforesaid FIR against the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there was a civil dispute between the partners of the firm, namely M/s. Gifted Hand Creation and the parties are the partners of the aforesaid firm.

The parties mutually decided to settle the dispute, and accordingly, the complainant had to pay Rs.
Ninety lakhs to the petitioners but could pay only Rs. 87,40,000/-, and to avoid the liability of the balance amount of Rs. 2,60,000/-, the complainant registered a false case against the petitioners.
5.

Learned counsel for the complainant submits that the petitioners, with the intention to cheat and misappropriate the funds of the complainant, entered into a conspiracy and caused an illegal loss of Rs. 87,40,000/- to the complainant and breached the trust by upsurging the amount mentioned above and after receipt of the aforesaid amount refused to register the sale deed in favour of the complainant as agreed.
6. The learned AGA submits that the impugned FIR was registered on 05.08.2023, and the investigation is at the initial stage.
The verification of the accounts to transfer the fund is yet to be investigated, and intervention of this Court at this stage would defeat the purpose of the investigation.
7. Be that as it may, on the reading of contents of the impugned FIR,prima facie,the commission of cognizable offence is made out against the petitioners.

Admittedly, there is a transfer of huge funds in the accounts of the petitioners through RTGS; the purpose and intent of such transfer need to be investigated, and the investigation is at the initial stage.
The petitioners could not invite the attention of the Court to anymala fideby the complainant.
In the facts-circumstances, no intervention is warranted by this Court at this stage.

8. And, also in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh), no case has been made out for interference with the impugned First Information Report.
